title: Keep your color
hookLine: whatever anyone does, I must be good, as an emerald keeps its color (Meditations 7.15)

cards: Drop an emerald in mud. Rinse it: green. Leave it in a dark drawer for years: green.
Insult it, praise it, sell it, steal it, put it in a crown or a junk shop. Still green. It doesn't change color depending on who's holding it.
Moods aren't like that. It's easy to go a little gray around gloomy people, a little sharp around sharp ones. Marcus Aurelius wanted to be more like the stone.

teach.b: Whatever anyone does or says, Marcus writes, I must be good, just as gold, or an emerald, or purple dye might always be saying: whatever anyone does or says, in George Long's translation, "I must be emerald and keep my colour."

Marcus doesn't explain the choice of those three. He lets each one speak, and all three say the same thing: I stay what I am. An emerald that turned brown when someone was rude to it wouldn't be much of an emerald.

teach.h: WHATEVER ANYONE DOES, I MUST BE GOOD.
teach.b: Notice the sentence begins with whatever anyone does or says. Marcus isn't hoping for kinder people. He takes their behavior as unpredictable, and moves all the responsibility to the one thing that's his: I must be good.

Your goodness isn't a reaction. It's your color. And look back at the week: love the people you're with, the dead philosophers, principles live, the idle show, the holy bond, member, not part, and now keep your color.
It's the week of other people, really: seven ways of staying yourself among them.
Not hard and cold, like a stone that shuts people out. Clear and steady, like a stone the light passes through.

how: Readers of Marcus often picture the emerald when they're provoked, as a reminder that their own goodness doesn't depend on how others behave.

o: a stone believed to bring luck to whoever holds it
a green gem that keeps its color whatever is done to it
a jewel that changes shade with its owner's mood

games.q: someone at work is sharp with you all morning. you feel yourself turning sharp too. what would the emerald do?
o: stay its own color: good, whatever they do.
games.why: Meditations 7.15: whatever anyone does or says, I must be emerald and keep my color.

practice: Hold in mind a person who tends to change your color, someone whose mood darkens yours or whose sharpness makes you sharp, and notice the familiar shift beginning. Picture an emerald in your palm, cool and green.
Stay your own shade of kind while they are whatever they are; no need to change them.

wordCard.voice: Emerald. Marcus says, whatever anyone does or says, I must be emerald and keep my color. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: keep my color. Whatever anyone does or says, the color is yours. A week done; see you tomorrow.
